\section{Non-Markovianity measurements}

Breuer--Laine--Piilo measure $\mathcal{N}$ (Eq.~\eqref{eq:ch3_blp}) on the idling register. First-layer trace distance in brackets.

\begin{itemize}
  \item non-Markovian production model, probe pair $|0\rangle$ vs. its partner: $\mathcal{N} = 0.8807$ (first layer $0.907$)
  \item non-Markovian production model, probe pair $|+\rangle$ vs. its partner: $\mathcal{N} = 0.8234$ (first layer $0.949$)
  \item reset control (defect reset every layer), probe pair $|0\rangle$ vs. its partner: $\mathcal{N} = 0.0000$ (first layer $0.907$)
  \item reset control (defect reset every layer), probe pair $|+\rangle$ vs. its partner: $\mathcal{N} = 0.0000$ (first layer $0.949$)
  \item defect-removed control, probe pair $|0\rangle$ vs. its partner: $\mathcal{N} = 0.0000$ (first layer $0.993$)
  \item defect-removed control, probe pair $|+\rangle$ vs. its partner: $\mathcal{N} = 0.0000$ (first layer $0.993$)
  \item coupling sweep ($g$, $\mathcal{N}$): (0.00, 0.0000), (0.05, 0.0000), (0.10, 0.5697), (0.15, 0.8807), (0.25, 1.6991), (0.40, 2.7005)
\end{itemize}

\section{Selected hyperparameters}

Cross-validated bandwidth and ridge penalty selected for the quantum-kernel arm on each split of the idealized-regime benchmark:

\begin{itemize}
  \item A random circuits: bandwidth $\beta = 0.15$, penalty $\alpha = 1.00e-04$
  \item B depth extrapolation: bandwidth $\beta = 0.15$, penalty $\alpha = 1.00e-04$
\end{itemize}
